# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)

Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.

**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.

## Layout

```
Devlog/
  README.md                  this file (the rules)
  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
```

## Rules for everyone (people and agents)

1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
   - **Cursor** (the art LAPTOP, which has no repo) is logged by user-level Cursor hooks instead: `Tools/Devlog/Install-CursorHooks.ps1` installs `cursor-devlog-hook.ps1`, which writes `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\cursor-<conversation>.jsonl` (plus transcripts). `Register-LaptopDevlogTasks.ps1` copies that folder every 10 minutes to `Incoming\LAPTOP\_devlog_raw` on CENTRAL, and CENTRAL's `JamDevlogImport` task (`Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1`) moves it into `Devlog/raw/`, where `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads it. The same kit runs on ASSETS (destination `Incoming\ASSETS\_devlog_raw`).
   - **Codex chats** (desktop app, IDE extension or interactive CLI, i.e. anything not launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`) on machines without the repo: before each sync, `Collect-CodexSessions.ps1` copies the session files Codex keeps in `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions` (full prompts, replies and tool calls) into `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\codex-*.jsonl`. `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads those too.
   - **Cursor transcripts:** `Collect-CursorTranscripts.ps1` also copies the full agent transcripts Cursor keeps in `%USERPROFILE%.cursorprojects*gent-transcripts`, so chats from before the hook was installed are not lost. The draft takes Cursor prompts from the transcript whenever there is one (it is complete; the hook missed some prompts before the mutex fix).
   - **Claude Code and Gemini CLI** on machines without the repo: `Collect-OtherAgents.ps1` copies their session files (`%USERPROFILE%.claudeprojects`, `%USERPROFILE%.gemini	mp`). OpenCode keeps its sessions in a SQLite database, so it is always launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`; on ASSETS the sync also sends that repo's `Devlogaw` (`-ExtraSource`).
   - **Size:** every collector strips base64 images (screenshots, renders) from the copies (`JamLogCopy.ps1`): one Codex session on ASSETS went from 110 MB to 4.2 MB with every message and tool call intact. `Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1` refuses files over 50 MB and logs them, because `Devlog/raw` goes to GitHub, which rejects files over 100 MB.
   - On CENTRAL, Codex and OpenCode always run through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`, so this collection is only needed on machines without the repo.
3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.

content.content:
<#
Smoke-Jam.ps1 - Runs the game by itself (console command "gb.Smoke": a scripted run of the main systems that
takes screenshots and quits) and reports what happened. It is NOT Play In Editor and nobody plays: it only
tells us whether the game starts, the systems run without crashing, and what the screen looks like.
A person still has to play the build.

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1              # uncooked game with the Editor binaries (-game)
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Packaged    # the packaged build in Glyphbound/Build/Windows
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only Entity -Offscreen   # only the Entity steps, no window
Output: the SMOKE lines, errors and warnings of our log category, and the list of screenshots.
Exit code: 0 = the script reached "SMOKE DONE" with no error lines and no crash.
#>
param(
    [switch]$Packaged,
    [string]$Only = '',      # filtered run: only the steps whose name starts with this (for example Entity), then quit
    [switch]$Offscreen,        # adds -RenderOffscreen: no window pops up
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 180,
    [int]$ResX = 1280,        # screenshot size (for example 1920 x 1080 to judge the HUD)
    [int]$ResY = 720
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$stamp = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')
$smokeCmd = if ($Only) { "gb.Smoke $Only" } else { 'gb.Smoke' }
$common = @('-windowed', "-ResX=$ResX", "-ResY=$ResY", '-unattended', '-nosplash', '-nosound', "-ExecCmds=`"$smokeCmd`"")
if ($Offscreen) { $common += '-RenderOffscreen' }
if ($Packaged) {
    $exe = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound.exe'
    if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) { Write-Host "No packaged build at $exe"; exit 2 }
    $shotDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound\Saved\Screenshots\Smoke'
    $log = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound\Saved\Logs\Glyphbound.log'
    $argList = $common
} else {
    $exe = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.exe'
    $shotDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Screenshots\Smoke'
    $log = Join-Path $projDir "Saved\Logs\smoke_$stamp.log"
    $argList = @("`"$Project`"", '-game', "-abslog=`"$log`"") + $common
}
if (Test-Path $shotDir) { Remove-Item (Join-Path $shotDir '*.png') -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $argList -PassThru
$timedOut = -not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)
if ($timedOut) {
    # This is the game process, not the Editor: stopping it is safe.
    Write-Host "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s: stopping the game process."
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Sleep 2
}
$sw.Stop()
if (-not (Test-Path $log)) { Write-Host "No log at $log (exit $($p.ExitCode))"; exit 2 }
$lines = Get-Content $log -Encoding UTF8
$smoke = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'SMOKE' })
$bad = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'LogGB: (Error|Warning)|Fatal error|Unhandled Exception|Assertion failed|Ensure condition failed|appError' })
$otherErrors = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match ': Error: ' -and $_ -notmatch 'LogGB' })
$smoke | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() }
Write-Host '---- problems in our code (LogGB warnings/errors, asserts, crashes) ----'
if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host '(none)' } else { $bad | Select-Object -First 40 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() } }
Write-Host "---- other engine errors: $($otherErrors.Count) ----"
$otherErrors | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() }
$shots = @(Get-ChildItem $shotDir -Filter *.png -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
Write-Host "---- screenshots: $($shots.Count) in $shotDir ----"
$shots | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_.Name }
$done = @($smoke | Where-Object { $_ -match 'SMOKE DONE' }).Count -gt 0
$crashed = @($bad | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Fatal error|Unhandled Exception|Assertion failed|appError' }).Count -gt 0
$errorCount = @($bad | Where-Object { $_ -match 'LogGB: Error' }).Count
Write-Host ("Smoke: done={0} crashed={1} LogGB errors={2} timedOut={3} wall={4:N0} s  log: {5}" -f $done, $crashed, $errorCount, $timedOut, $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, $log)
if ($done -and -not $crashed -and $errorCount -eq 0 -and -not $timedOut) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }

---
name: machine-lock-shared
description: GameJam CENTRAL runs several Claude chats at once; builds/game runs must honor Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c499171-af23-4e77-afe4-86028ce8f216
  modified: 2026-11-13T12:45:40.406Z
---

On CENTRAL several architect chats work on the repo at the same time (seen 2026-11-13: the HUD chat and the GBPixelVfx chat). They share one rule: one build or game run at a time, signalled by `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock` ("who | what | UTC time"; a lock younger than 45 min means wait). `Tools/Jam/PixelVfx-Jam.ps1` implements the wait; `Build-Jam.ps1` and `Smoke-Jam.ps1` do not, so wrap them yourself.

**Why:** a concurrent `Smoke-Jam.ps1` deletes the other chat's screenshots, and a concurrent build fails with "file in use"; the other chat's half-written edits can also break your build for a few minutes.

**How to apply:** before building or running the game, check the lock and running cl.exe/UnrealEditor processes; take the lock while you run. When other chats have uncommitted edits in shared files (GDD.md, GBDevCommands.cpp, Build.cs), commit only your hunks: stage "HEAD + your change" with `git hash-object -w --stdin` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`, never `git add` their files. See [[commit-changes-always]].

---

On CENTRAL several architect chats work on the repo at the same time (seen 2026-11-13: the HUD chat and the GBPixelVfx chat). They share one rule: one build or game run at a time, signalled by `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock` ("who | what | UTC time"; a lock younger than 45 min means wait). `Tools/Jam/PixelVfx-Jam.ps1` implements the wait; `Build-Jam.ps1` and `Smoke-Jam.ps1` do not, so wrap them yourself.

**Why:** a concurrent `Smoke-Jam.ps1` deletes the other chat's screenshots, and a concurrent build fails with "file in use"; the other chat's half-written edits can also break your build for a few minutes.

**How to apply:** before building or running the game, check the lock and running cl.exe/UnrealEditor processes; take the lock while you run. When other chats have uncommitted edits in shared files (GDD.md, GBDevCommands.cpp, Build.cs), commit only your hunks: stage "HEAD + your change" with `git hash-object -w --stdin` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`, never `git add` their files. See [[commit-changes-always]].

<#
Build-Jam.ps1 - Compiles the Glyphbound C++ module (Editor target by default) and prints only what matters.
One build at a time per machine: do not run this while another build, a package or a test run is going.
The Editor must be closed (a full build cannot link while the Editor holds the DLLs).

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1                 # GlyphboundEditor Win64 Development
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound   # game target

Output: full log in Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/build_last.log; the console shows errors (first 60) and the result line.
Exit code: 0 = Result: Succeeded.
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Target = 'GlyphboundEditor',
    [string]$Config = 'Development',
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$MaxErrors = 60
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$logDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($logDir)
$log = Join-Path $logDir 'build_last.log'
$bat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat'
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$bat`" $Target Win64 $Config -project=`"$Project`" -waitmutex > `"$log`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()
$errors = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern '(: error |: fatal error |error LNK|Error: |ERROR: |UHT.*[Ee]rror)' | Select-Object -First $MaxErrors

# Code review: shotgun pump rack and reload pose, Glyphbound (UE 5.9, C++)

You are reviewing, read-only, a small change to the shotgun's first-person viewmodel. Run `git diff HEAD --
Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Weapons/GBGun.cpp Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Core/GBDevCommands.cpp` and read the
surrounding code in `GBGun.cpp` (struct `FGBGunModelArt`, `ApplyPump`, `ApplyViewModelPose`, `ApplyReloadMagazine`,
the Tick part with the visual timers) and `UI/GBHUD.cpp` (the gun branch of the hands drawing, around
`GetPumpHandShift`). Ignore other modified files (Devlog raw logs).

What changed:
1. The pump's "rack" motion of the whole gun was a dip (float cm) and a roll (float deg). It is now a full offset
   (`FVector PumpRackOffset`, camera frame) and rotation (`FRotator PumpRackRot`) scaled by the pump amount, so the
   gun can be pulled in, tip its muzzle up, turn and roll to show the forend. Only the shotgun sets them (the pistol
   and rifle initializers stop before the pump fields and must stay at zero).
2. New art values for the shotgun: rack offset/rotation, left-hand travel with the pump, reload pose offset and
   rotation (roll 130 degrees so the loading port on the underside faces the camera), left-hand reach and right-hand
   follow during the reload.
3. The pump timer now advances by the clamped `EffectStep` (max 1/30 s per frame) instead of the raw `DeltaSeconds`,
   like the kick and muzzle-flash timers, so a hitch right after a shot cannot skip the whole rack.
4. Smoke script (`gb.Smoke`, shotgun block): the shot step moved from SG+0.9 to SG+1.1 s, the mid-pump check from
   +1.27 to +1.47, the "home again" check from +1.85 to +1.8, so the shot no longer lands in the frame that pays for
   the previous step's screenshot (a ~0.5 s hitch that skipped the pump in a filtered run).

## What to look for (ranked)
1. Real bugs: wrong composition of the rack with the kick and reload pose (`Root->SetRelativeLocation/Rotation`),
   the rack or the reload pose not returning exactly to rest (the smoke checks the root is within 0.05 cm and 0.5 deg
   of rest after the pump, after a reload and after a cancel), a pistol or rifle that now gets a non-zero rack, a
   reload magazine drop direction that breaks with a 130 degree roll (`ApplyReloadMagazine` unrotates "camera down"
   through the root rotation), FRotator scaling (`FRotator * float`) or wrap-around issues at large angles.
2. Timing: with the clamped step, can the pump still be moving (or stuck back) when the next shot is allowed, or
   when a reload begins, a weapon switch happens, or the game is paused? Is anything else reading `PumpElapsed` with
   the assumption that it tracks real time?
3. Smoke step timing: after the move, are the step comments and checks still true (the "home again before the next
   shot is allowed" step at 0.7 s after the shot, with FireInterval 0.8 and the pump home at 0.72 of it), and does
   anything later in the block depend on the shot's old time?

Do not suggest style rewrites, renames or new features, and do not judge the art values themselves (they were
tuned from screenshots). For each finding give: file:line, what goes wrong, a concrete scenario, and a fix. If you
find nothing real, say so plainly.

## Thirty-third block: the shotgun plays: model, pump and shell-by-shell reload
**Who did what.** Claude Sonnet 5.5 (subagent, 23 minutes of work in two runs) wrote the code from the brief. GPT Sol 6.1 (Codex CLI, medium, read-only, logged run `061745-codex-de1c36`) reviewed it. The architect (Claude Fable 5.2) wrote the brief and the review prompt, read the screenshots, ran the final checks and packaged.

**What was built** (`Weapons/GBGun.*`, 433 lines changed in the `.cpp`):
- **Model:** a third entry in the gun art table, `ShotgunArt`, with a new optional part, the pump. The pistol's and the rifle's entries leave the new fields at zero.
- **Pump:** after each shot it slides back 4.2 cm and returns, as shares of the time between shots; the gun dips and rolls a little and the 2D left hand rides it. Only the look: no gameplay timing changed.
- **Shell-by-shell reload:** the stepping is a small plain struct, `FGBPerRoundReload` (begin, advance, stop), with no world in it, so it can be tested. One shell takes `ReloadTime / MagazineSize`; a long frame moves several shells and keeps the leftover time. The reserve of such a gun is counted in rounds inside the same field the other guns use for magazines; every reader of that field was listed and checked (equipment's full ammo, pickups, inventory, HUD).
- **Its look:** the reload pose and the hand beats of the magazine guns, repeated once per shell: the shell rises from under the view, slides into the port, a bump seats it.
- **HUD:** the reserve reads `x24 shells`.
- **Data:** `"ViewModel": "Shotgun"` and `"ReloadPerRound": 1` on the shotgun in `Weapons.json`.

**The owner's new rule arrived while the implementer was running** (`CLAUDE.md`, "Tiempo de iteración": while iterating, only the filtered smoke with no window and Editor-target builds; the full smoke and the game build once, at the end). The architect sent it to the running subagent as a message and added it to the brief. The subagent had already run one full smoke by then; after the message it ran only `Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only shotgun -Offscreen` (25 to 31 s against 107 s for the full run).

**Sol's review: five findings, all fixed by Sonnet in a second run.**
1. A tap on fire during the reload of an empty shotgun lost the shot: releasing the trigger cleared the pending shot, so the player had to hold the button.
2. Pressing fire right after a shot did not stop the reload until the time between shots had passed, because the base class checks the fire rate before it asks the gun anything. The gun now handles the press itself.
3. With a shot pending on an empty gun, one long frame could load several shells before the shot was looked at. The stepping takes a maximum number of rounds now, and a pending shot asks for one.
4. Cancelling a reload early made the 2D hands jump towards the full reload pose: the blend started from 1 whatever the pose was. It starts from the pose at the cancel.
5. **The four new tests let wrong code pass.** Sol named, for each, an implementation that was wrong and still green: a total stretched to 2.02 s (the last sample was at 2.03), a cycle computed from the rounds planned instead of the capacity (the only step was ten seconds long), a remainder computed with a modulo (never checked after the second call), a cycle computed from the empty space (never checked at the first shell's boundary). Each test now checks one millisecond before and exactly at the boundary. The project's rule "each test must be able to fail" was in the brief, and the first tests still did not meet it.
- Solid by Sol's reading: the reserve's conversion, pickups, inventory, stored guns, refills, the divisions by zero, the cook of the meshes, and the pistol's and rifle's paths.

**What the architect saw in the game's screenshots** (`20a` to `20e`):
- The gun sits in the lower right, the barrel's line runs to the crosshair, the ammo hologram in the sight's window reads `6` with its six pips.
- **The energy bar cannot be read.** On top of the receiver the camera sees it almost edge-on (`19a`). Lowering the gun to look down on it put it behind the 2D hands. The architect made its place a switch in the build script, built the other place (the sight's rear lower panel, which faces the player), rendered it (`19b`, `19c`) and asked. Owner: "Déjala en el cajón" ("Leave it on the receiver"). It stays; the switch stays off.
- The pump is under the gun and is hardly seen from the first-person camera; the rack motion and the left hand carry it.
- In the reload pose the gun shows its side more than its underside, so the port is barely in view and the shell is small. The pose still uses the rifle's starting values.

**Final checks, once each** (holding the machine lock agreed with the pixel-art VFX chat, `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock`):
- Import again from the rebuilt `Shotgun.blend`: `OK` in 18 s; the strip's six face corners run from 0 to 1.
- Full smoke: 138 steps, `done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0`, 107 s. The 38 pistol, rifle and gun lines are identical to the last full run before the shotgun's code (compared with the step numbers and times stripped).
- Game target build: succeeded, 49 s. Full test suite: 43 run, 0 failed, 0.71 s of test time.
- Package `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`: **277.1 MB**. The packaged game passes the shotgun's filtered smoke with its 6 meshes, so the art was cooked.
  - **Correction, later the same day (found by the pixel-art VFX chat while packaging `6062d97`):** this package very likely showed the boss with its placeholder look. The Entity's art is loaded by path, and its folder (`/Game/Glyphbound/Enemies`) was not in `DirectoriesToAlwaysCook` at this commit (`e1ac783`), so the cook left it out; the code then keeps the placeholder and logs a warning, not an error. The check above could not see it: on the packaged game only the shotgun's filtered smoke was run, and a missing-art warning does not count in `LogGB errors=0`. Not confirmed on this zip itself, which the next package replaced (299.7 MB, with the folder added to the cook list). Lesson: a filtered smoke on the package proves only the part it filters; art that is loaded by path needs its folder in the cook list, like `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons` has.

**Needs a person playing:** the pump's and the reload's timing and feel, the hands, firing right after the last shell, and whether the shotgun's size feels right next to the rifle.
- **Implementer:** Sonnet, not Muse Spark: the owner's choice for the gun models' code.

- `media/2026-11-12/17a_shotgun_source_first_person.png`, `17b_shotgun_source_close.png`, `17c_shotgun_source_left.png`, `17d_shotgun_source_screen.png` (twenty-sixth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): the shotgun's Tripo source untouched, from the player's camera, close up, from the left, and its side screen.
- `media/2026-11-12/17e_shotgun_cables_receiver.png`, `17f_shotgun_cables_receiver_unlit.png`, `17g_shotgun_cables_front_unlit.png`, `17h_shotgun_cables_player_eye.png`, `17i_shotgun_cables_found.png` (twenty-sixth block; Blender Cycles renders of the re-exported GLB, not the game): the cable bundle on the receiver lit and unlit (texels as they are), the front bundle unlit with its imprint on the body, the receiver bundle from the player's eye, and the four cable groups painted red on a grey gun.
- `media/2026-11-12/17j_shotgun_rebuilt_first_person.png`, `17k_shotgun_rebuilt_close.png`, `17l_shotgun_rebuilt_front.png`, `17m_shotgun_rebuilt_rear.png`, `17n_shotgun_rebuilt_left.png` (twenty-ninth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): the shotgun after the rebuild, from the player's camera, close up, from the front and the rear three-quarters, and from the left.
- `media/2026-11-12/17o_shotgun_parts_first_person.png`, `17p_shotgun_ammo_hologram.png`, `17q_shotgun_energy_bar.png`, `17r_shotgun_parts_left.png`, `17s_shotgun_port_and_shell.png`, `17t_shotgun_pump_back.png`, `17u_shotgun_parts_rear.png` (twenty-ninth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): the shotgun with its functional parts: from the player's camera, the ammo hologram in the sight's window, the energy bar's 13 cells, the left side, the loading port with a shell on its way out, the pump at the back of its travel, and the rear three-quarters.
- `media/2026-11-12/17v_shotgun_cell_canister.png`, `17w_shotgun_cell_side.png`, `17x_shotgun_side_plate.png`, `17y_shotgun_side_plate_right.png`, `17z_shotgun_notes_first_person.png` (thirtieth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): after the owner's notes: the cell as a canister in its bay (the owner's own view of it, and from the side), the left and right side plates that replace the screens, and the player's camera.
- `media/2026-11-12/18a_shotgun_review_first_person.png` to `18g_shotgun_review_right.png` (thirtieth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): after the architect's own review: the player's camera close up, the cell and side plate, the stock, the receiver, the top, the rear three-quarters and the right side. `18h_shotgun_review_stock_before.png`, `18i_shotgun_review_receiver_before.png`, `18j_shotgun_review_top_before.png`: the stock, the receiver and the top before that review.
- `media/2026-11-12/18k_shotgun_plate_straight.png`, `18l_shotgun_plate_straight_right.png`, `18m_shotgun_plate_owner_view.png` (thirtieth block; Blender Cycles renders, not the game): the side plates with their border following the face's four real edges, left and right, and from the owner's angle.
- `media/2026-11-12/19a_shotgun_ingame_bar_edge_on.png` (thirty-third block; the game's smoke run, enlarged three times): the shotgun in the game, its energy bar seen edge-on on top of the receiver. `19b_shotgun_bar_on_sight_panel.png`, `19c_shotgun_bar_on_sight_first_person.png` (Blender Cycles renders, not the game, not imported): the place the architect proposed for the bar, on the sight's rear panel, which the owner declined.
- `media/2026-11-12/20a_shotgun_game_hip.png`, `20b_shotgun_game_pump.png`, `20c_shotgun_game_enchanted.png`, `20d_shotgun_game_reload_shell.png`, `20e_shotgun_game_four_crops.png` (thirty-third block; the full smoke run of the editor build): the shotgun at the hip, with the pump pinned back, with an ice enchant, with a shell on its way into the port, and the gun's area of the four side by side.

# Block: the shotgun's pump and reload made readable (Nov 13, CENTRAL)

> Written by the architect chat of this block (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). To be merged into the day entry by whoever closes the day. Times in UTC.

## Where it started
The shotgun chat (thirty-third block, Nov 12 entry) ended with a list of weak points. The owner pasted that list into a new chat. Of its four items, two were work for the architect:
- **The pump** was under the gun, out of sight of the first-person camera. Its "rack" was a 0.5 cm dip and a 1.5 degree roll, which nobody could see.
- **The reload pose** showed the gun's side, not its underside, so the loading port was barely in view and the shell looked tiny. It still used the rifle's starting values.

The other two stay as they were. The energy bar on the receiver is the owner's decision. Only a person playing can judge the feel.

## What changed (`Weapons/GBGun.cpp`, `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
- **The rack is now a full motion.** The two floats became an offset (`FVector PumpRackOffset`, camera frame) and a rotation (`FRotator PumpRackRot`), both scaled by how far back the pump is. While the pump is back, the gun is pulled in 2 cm, tips its muzzle up 7 degrees, turns 10 degrees to the left and rolls 12 degrees. That shows the forend with its glyph to the camera. The 2D left hand now moves down with the pull (art pixels `(-4, 6)`, before `(-6, 1)`). The pistol and the rifle leave these fields at zero.
- **Reload pose.** The gun rolls 130 degrees, which turns it almost over, and lifts its muzzle 15 degrees. The loading port on the underside, with its glowing ring and the shell going in, now faces the camera near the middle of the screen. The left hand reaches up under the port (`(12, -24)`, before `(0, -2)`).
- **Smoke timing (a flaky check fixed).** The first filtered run failed `shotgun pump: slid back during the interval` with the pump at 0.00 cm. This was not caused by the new values. The screenshot taken just before the shot stalled one frame for about 0.5 s. The shot was fired in that same frame, so the gun's next tick got the whole stalled time at once and the pump went back and home inside it. The shot step moved from 0.9 s to 1.1 s into the block, so it no longer shares that frame. The mid-pump check moved with it (0.37 s after the shot, as before). The "home again" check now runs 0.7 s after the shot: the pump is home at 0.576 s, and the next shot is allowed at 0.8 s.

## How the pose was found: eight build-and-screenshot rounds
Each round compiled the Editor target (13 to 43 s), ran `Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only shotgun -Offscreen` (about 65 s) and cropped the gun's area. Each run held the shared `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock`. Round by round:
1. Roll 80, gun pulled towards the camera: huge on screen, still the side (`shotgun_pose_reload_try_it1.png`).
2. Roll 115, muzzle up 20: the trigger guard shows, but the gun covers the left half of the screen (`try_it2`).
3. Roll 105, pushed forward, turned left: the underside faces left, away from the camera, which sits to the gun's right (`try_it3`).
4. The geometry, worked out: the camera is behind, above and to the left of the gun. For the port to face it, the underside has to point back, up and left. That calls for a roll of about 130 degrees plus some muzzle-up pitch. Roll 130 with pitch 28 got the port into view, but the gun stood almost vertical (`try_it4`).
5. Pitch 15: the gun lies diagonally, the port and shell sit near the centre (`try_it5`), kept.
6. to 8. Hands: the right hand first slid onto the left one; the final values keep the right hand on the receiver and put the left hand under the port.

## Review: GPT Sol 6.1 (Codex CLI, medium, read-only, logged through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`)
Prompt: `Prompts/shotgun_poses_review_sol.md`. **One real finding, fixed.** The first version also made the pump timer advance by the clamped visual step (at most 1/30 s per frame, like the kick and the muzzle flash), so that a stall could not skip the rack. Sol showed what that breaks: at 15 fps the pump needs about 1.15 s to come home, but the next shot is allowed after 0.8 s, so the pump would snap back when the player fires again. The pump timer is back on real time. A comment in the code says why. Sol found nothing else: the pose returns to rest, the pistol and the rifle get no rack, and the falling shell still drops straight down on screen at a 130 degree roll.

## Checks
- Full smoke, once, at the end: `done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0`, 58 screenshots, 142 s. Then, after Sol's fix, the shotgun's filtered smoke: pump 4.15 cm from rest at 0.37 s after the shot, everything back at rest after it, 0 errors.
- Tests: 44 run, 0 failed (1.00 s of test time, 27 s of wall time).
- Game target build: succeeded (41 s; 26 s again after the fix).
- **Not packaged in this block.** Nobody has played it yet.

## Implementer
The architect made these edits directly, not Muse Spark. It was a handful of art constants and a two-field struct change, tuned by looking at screenshots one round at a time. Handing each round to an implementer would have cost more than the change itself.

## Screenshots (`media/2026-11-13/`, the game's smoke run, editor build, gun area enlarged 1.4 times)
- `shotgun_pose_pump_before.png` / `shotgun_pose_pump_after.png`: the pump pinned at the back of its travel, before (Nov 12 run, old HUD) and after. The forend now turns towards the camera.
- `shotgun_pose_reload_before.png` / `shotgun_pose_reload_after.png`: a shell's cycle pinned mid-way, before and after. `shotgun_pose_reload_after_full.png`: the whole screen after.
- `shotgun_pose_reload_try_it1.png` to `try_it5.png` (half size): the rounds of the search above.

## Needs a person playing
Whether the rack's turn feels like a pump or like the gun waving, how the 130 degree turn plays when it repeats for every shell (it holds the pose between shells), and the hands.

Each round compiled the Editor target (13 to 43 s), ran `Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only shotgun -Offscreen` (about 65 s) and cropped the gun's area. Each run held the shared `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock`. Round by round:
1. Roll 80, gun pulled towards the camera: huge on screen, still the side (`shotgun_pose_reload_try_it1.png`).
2. Roll 115, muzzle up 20: the trigger guard shows, but the gun covers the left half of the screen (`try_it2`).
3. Roll 105, pushed forward, turned left: the underside faces left, away from the camera, which sits to the gun's right (`try_it3`).
4. The geometry, worked out: the camera is behind, above and to the left of the gun. For the port to face it, the underside has to point back, up and left. That calls for a roll of about 130 degrees plus some muzzle-up pitch. Roll 130 with pitch 28 got the port into view, but the gun stood almost vertical (`try_it4`).
5. Pitch 15: the gun lies diagonally, the port and shell sit near the centre (`try_it5`), kept.
6. to 8. Hands: the right hand first slid onto the left one; the final values keep the right hand on the receiver and put the left hand under the port.

## Review: GPT Sol 6.1 (Codex CLI, medium, read-only, logged through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`)
Prompt: `Prompts/shotgun_poses_review_sol.md`. **One real finding, fixed.** The first version also made the pump timer advance by the clamped visual step (at most 1/30 s per frame, like the kick and the muzzle flash), so that a stall could not skip the rack. Sol showed what that breaks: at 15 fps the pump needs about 1.15 s to come home, but the next shot is allowed after 0.8 s, so the pump would snap back when the player fires again. The pump timer is back on real time. A comment in the code says why. Sol found nothing else: the pose returns to rest, the pistol and the rifle get no rack, and the falling shell still drops straight down on screen at a 130 degree roll.

## Checks
- Full smoke, once, at the end: `done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0`, 58 screenshots, 142 s. Then, after Sol's fix, the shotgun's filtered smoke: pump 4.15 cm from rest at 0.37 s after the shot, everything back at rest after it, 0 errors.
- Tests: 44 run, 0 failed (1.00 s of test time, 27 s of wall time).
- Game target build: succeeded (41 s; 26 s again after the fix).
- **Not packaged in this block.** Nobody has played it yet.

## Implementer
The architect made these edits directly, not Muse Spark. It was a handful of art constants and a two-field struct change, tuned by looking at screenshots one round at a time. Handing each round to an implementer would have cost more than the change itself.

## Screenshots (`media/2026-11-13/`, the game's smoke run, editor build, gun area enlarged 1.4 times)
- `shotgun_pose_pump_before.png` / `shotgun_pose_pump_after.png`: the pump pinned at the back of its travel, before (Nov 12 run, old HUD) and after. The forend now turns towards the camera.
- `shotgun_pose_reload_before.png` / `shotgun_pose_reload_after.png`: a shell's cycle pinned mid-way, before and after. `shotgun_pose_reload_after_full.png`: the whole screen after.
- `shotgun_pose_reload_try_it1.png` to `try_it5.png` (half size): the rounds of the search above.

## Needs a person playing
Whether the rack's turn feels like a pump or like the gun waving, how the 130 degree turn plays when it repeats for every shell (it holds the pose between shells), and the hands.

De los cuatro pendientes que dejó el otro chat, arreglé los dos que se podían arreglar: la corredera y la pose de recarga. Los otros dos siguen como estaban: la barra de energía queda en el cajón porque así lo decidiste, y lo de jugarla tiene que hacerlo una persona. Está en `b2c1966` y subido a `origin main`.

## Qué cambió
- **Corredera:** antes el arma solo bajaba medio centímetro, y no se notaba. Ahora, mientras la corredera va atrás, el arma se acerca, sube un poco la boca del cañón, gira a la izquierda y se ladea. Así se ve la parte delantera, con su glifo. La mano izquierda baja con el tirón.
- **Recarga:** el arma se gira casi del revés (130°) y sube la boca 15°. El puerto de carga queda de cara a la cámara, cerca del centro: se ve su aro brillante y el cartucho entrando. La mano izquierda se pone justo debajo del puerto. Encontré la pose en ocho rondas de compilar, sacar capturas y corregir; las rondas están en la bitácora.
- **Prueba automática:** la comprobación de la corredera falló al principio con 0 cm, y no era por mis valores. La captura anterior congela un fotograma medio segundo y el disparo caía en ese mismo fotograma, así que la corredera iba y volvía de golpe. Moví el disparo de la prueba 0,2 s más tarde.

## Verificación
- **Revisión de Sol 6.1:** un hallazgo real, ya corregido. Mi primera versión limitaba cuánto avanza el tiempo de la corredera en cada fotograma. Por debajo de 30 fps eso la habría dejado atrás cuando ya toca disparar otra vez. Volví a usar el tiempo real.
- **Prueba automática completa:** 0 errores y 58 capturas. Después del arreglo de Sol pasé otra vez la prueba de la escopeta sola, también sin errores.
- **Tests:** los 44 en verde. Las compilaciones del Editor y del juego también salen bien.
- **Bitácora:** el bloque está en [2026-11-13_shotgun_poses_block.md](Devlog/days/2026-11-13_shotgun_poses_block.md), con capturas de antes y después en `Devlog/media/2026-11-13/`.

## Lo que falta
- **Sin empaquetar.**
- **Sin jugar:** falta ver si el giro de la corredera parece un bombeo de verdad o el arma bailando. También cómo se siente la pose de recarga cuando se repite con cada cartucho, y si las manos quedan bien.
- **Un aviso de GitHub al subir:** una transcripción de `Devlog/raw` ya pesa 67 MB. GitHub rechaza archivos de más de 100 MB, así que conviene vigilarla.
